Triage agent

Triage agent setup

Sign-in works

Triage agent: Codex with an API key, model test-model, reasoning effort high.

Set up by administrator at 1 Jan 1970 00:00.

Sign-in to Codex works. Last checked at 12:00.

MMHotline checks the sign-in once a day with the setup test's prompt, unless a run of the triage agent succeeded in the last 24 hours, and tells administrators when the sign-in fails and when the sign-in works again.

The triage agent investigates SOS incidents before MMHotline wakes a person. The rules for running the agent's playbooks decide which fixes need approval.

How setup is checked

The coding agent, its credential, its model, and its reasoning effort are tested before they apply: MMHotline runs one test prompt with them, and keeps the earlier setup when the test fails. Codex takes an API key, a Codex access token, or a ChatGPT sign-in made just for MMHotline; Claude Code an API key or its subscription token from claude setup-token.

Run limit

Runs that count toward the run limit in the last 24 hours: 1 of 50.

The limit counts the runs MMHotline starts by itself: triage sessions' runs, scheduled software reviews, and commit reviews. It stops only agent runs, never alerts. Set it with triage_agent.most_runs_in_24_hours in the settings file.

Software review

Scheduled software review: off. The triage agent wakes only for alerts.

What the software review does

The software review starts the triage agent with the team's task from scheduled_software_review_task.md in the systems repository, such as checking the servers' packages and programs for known flaws. Each finding reaches people as a report at its alert severity. Each review costs one run of the coding agent. To turn the scheduled review on, add the task file and set triage_agent.software_review_interval_hours in the settings file. To start one review now, such as to learn what a review costs, run sudo mmhotline triage-agent run-software-review on the server.

Commit review

When the settings let the triage agent approve, MMHotline starts a commit review run for each commit no trusted key signed that the triage agent may review. The agent approves an ordinary change, or decides that a person must review the commit; the decisions are on the Approvals page.

Review agent

Not set up

Review agent: not set up

To add a second coding agent that reviews proposed playbooks, set review_agent in the settings file.

How playbook review works

A review agent is a second coding agent. When a review agent is set up, the review agent must approve each playbook the triage agent asks to run before the rules for running the agent's playbooks apply. When the review agent refuses a playbook, the refusal reason goes back to the triage agent, which may revise the playbook and ask again. After the review agent's third refusal in a row on a problem, a person decides. Each review is a fresh run in the triage agent's sandbox, in a new empty home directory: the review agent sees the playbook and the triage agent's diagnosis, never the logs, and reaches only the review agent's coding agent service.

Any coding agent can review, the triage agent's own included. A coding agent of another vendor than the triage agent's is recommended: its model is less likely to share the triage agent's mistakes, and like every review agent it never sees the logs that could mislead the triage agent.

Internet access and connections

Internet access

Listed hosts only. The triage agent reaches the internet only through MMHotline's logging proxy.

Listed hosts

At the start of each run in the systems repository, MMHotline lists each server of its inventories at port 22, so the triage agent can read the servers over SSH. It also lists the host of each vendor page in software_outside_the_distribution.yml, each program's releases_page and security_advisories_page, so the software review can read them. The servers and the vendor pages' hosts below were listed at the start of the latest run, 12:00; a server or a page removed since stays listed until the next run.
